title: Reading One Motor in a Trap

scenes.tts: One kinesin molecule rides a bead along a microtubule in a dish. It moves in jumps of eight nanometres. At low load, each jump costs one A T P. These numbers come from purified proteins, in vitro. But how do you watch one molecule step?
scenes.caption: One kinesin molecule rides a bead along a microtubule in a dish. It moves in jumps of 8 nanometres. At low load, each jump costs one ATP. These numbers come from purified proteins, in vitro. But how do you watch one molecule step?
scenes.visual: Microtubule bar with a bead carried by one kinesin that jumps in 8 nm steps; a green ATP chip is spent at each jump; a question mark replaces the picture of how to watch it.
scenes.narration: One kinesin molecule rides a bead along a microtubule in a dish. It moves in jumps of 8 nanometres. At low load, each jump costs one ATP. These numbers come from purified proteins, in vitro. But how do you watch one molecule step?

scenes.tts: A gliding assay usually shows many motors at once. To see one, use an optical trap. A focused laser holds a small bead near its centre. Pull the bead off centre, and the trap pulls it back, like a weight on a spring. The force is the trap stiffness, kappa, times the distance from the centre.

scenes.visual: Many motors push a filament in a gliding assay, then one bead sits in a laser trap, is pulled off centre, and a spring and force arrow appear with F = κx.

scenes.tts: Here is a worked problem, with made up data in the range of real measurements. At low load, the bead moves four hundred nanometres in half a second. That is eight hundred nanometres per second. Divide by the eight nanometre step, and you get one hundred steps per second. Near zero load, kinesin uses one A T P per step. So this motor burns about one hundred A T P every second.
scenes.caption: Here is a worked problem, with made-up data in the range of real measurements. At low load, the bead moves 400 nanometres in half a second. That is 800 nanometres per second. Divide by the 8-nanometre step, and you get 100 steps per second. Near zero load, kinesin uses one ATP per step. So this motor burns about 100 ATP every second.
scenes.visual: A staircase of position against time rises to 400 nm at 0.5 s; the arithmetic 400/0.5 = 800 nm/s and 800/8 = 100 steps/s appears, then one ATP per step gives about 100 ATP per second.

scenes.tts: Now let the bead pull against the trap. The trap stiffness is zero point zero five piconewtons per nanometre. The motor walks until it stalls, with the bead one hundred twenty nanometres from the centre. Force is stiffness times distance. That is six piconewtons, at the top of the range that was measured, five to six.
scenes.caption: Now let the bead pull against the trap. The trap stiffness is 0.05 piconewtons per nanometre. The motor walks until it stalls, with the bead 120 nanometres from the centre. Force is stiffness times distance. That is 6 piconewtons, at the top of the range that was measured, 5 to 6.
scenes.visual: The bead steps away from the trap centre, the spring stretches and the force arrow grows until the bead stalls 120 nm out; F = 0.05 x 120 = 6 pN, marked at the top of a 5 to 6 pN range.
scenes.narration: Now let the bead pull against the trap. The trap stiffness is 0.05 piconewtons per nanometre. The motor walks until it stalls, with the bead 120 nanometres from the centre. scenes.tts: How much work is that? Work per step is force times distance. Six piconewtons times eight nanometres is forty eight piconewton nanometres. Assume that one mole of A T P releases about fifty kilojoules. That is eighty three piconewton nanometres for each molecule. The true value depends on the concentrations of A T P, A D P and phosphate. Near stall, forty eight over eighty three is about fifty eight percent.
scenes.caption: How much work is that? Work per step is force times distance. 6 piconewtons times 8 nanometres is 48 piconewton-nanometres. Assume that one mole of ATP releases about 50 kilojoules. That is 83 piconewton-nanometres for each molecule. The true value depends on the concentrations of ATP, ADP and phosphate. Near stall, 48 over 83 is about 58 percent.
scenes.visual: A rectangle 6 pN tall and 8 nm wide gives 48 pN nm; it fills most of a bar of 83 pN nm (one ATP, about 50 kJ per mole, with the hedge) and the fraction 58 percent appears.

scenes.tts: Two cautions. The bead moves as far as the motor only if the link between them is stiff. A floppy tether stretches, and the bead under-reports the step. And never combine numbers from different experiments. One muscle myosin moved its filament about eleven nanometres at low load. Held still, it pulled with three to four piconewtons. Those are two loading conditions. Keep every number tied to the preparation that measured it.
